A January 2026 Rift Valley Institute conference report confirms social-assistance delivery mechanisms continue to operate in a fragmented, region-specific way amid the conflict (e.g. mobile cash in RSF-held areas, ID-linked public works in SAF areas), with explicit recommendations to make 'registries and databases interoperable.' This confirms a genuine, named, partially-implemented system existed before the 2023 conflict and some form of registry-based delivery persists, but continuity and current national coverage are uncertain amid war-driven fragmentation. Score raised from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Under development) rather than a higher score, given this uncertainty.
revised_comments: Sudan's Ministry of Labour and Social Development operates a Social Safety Net Management Information System, developed with World Bank support, comprising a centralised poverty registry, targeting and eligibility module, grievance-redress module, payment module and monitoring and evaluation module. Originally deployed in six of Sudan's eighteen states with plans to scale nationally, the register's rollout was partial before the 2023 conflict, and social-assistance delivery has since become fragmented across conflict-affected regions, with calls to restore registry interoperability.
